events.title: FORTRAN 77 standard approved (ANSI X3.9-1978)
events.summary: ANSI approved the FORTRAN 77 standard on April 3, 1978 — the revision that introduced structured control flow to scientific computing.
events.about: FORTRAN 77 added `IF`/`ELSE`, `DO` loops with `END DO`, and character strings — making large scientific codebases maintainable. It became the baseline for decades of HPC, weather models, and engineering simulation. Many legacy `.f77` files still run in production clusters.

narrative.whyChosen: FORTRAN 77 is the standard most programmers mean when they say 'classic Fortran' before the 90 rewrite.
narrative.whyImportant: It brought structured programming to the dominant scientific language without breaking the formula-centric style researchers relied on.
narrative.problemSolved: FORTRAN 66 lacked modern control structures; portable scientific code needed a stable, vendor-neutral revision.
